correctness.rationale: Exact absorbing-interval Laplace transforms give the image-series fluxes. The leading images, the complementary-error-function expansion and the \(c_N\) normalization yield the two limiting intensities \(e^{-y}\) and \(e^{-2\theta-y}\). Differentiated fluxes yield the normalized and factorized marked Gumbel density. IID renewal with episode durations tending to one on the \(b/\log N\) scale yields the geometric total-time law. A two-scale exit-survival bound ensures \(\mathbb E[(\log N)T_N/b]\to1\), providing the mean identity. The standalone numerical checker evaluates 12 parameter/population pairs, 36 centered distribution-function values, four exact midpoint symmetries and three Laplace-transform identities. It does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The principal 2026 model paper has general finite-N renewal laws and fixed-distance asymptotics. The 2021 rigorous extreme-hitting theorem presupposes strictly distinct fixed large-deviation exponents, and the 2010 exact box-exit formula does not state the moving-threshold joint time/mark and geometric restarted completion limit. value.rationale: The absorbing boundaries compete on the natural \(O(1/\log N)\) displacement scale not resolved by fixed unequal-distance asymptotics. The theorem establishes a nondegenerate logistic target-selection transition, the jointly independent Gumbel endpoint mark, a geometric normalized completion-time law and its exact leading mean coefficient for a physical collective-reset protocol. This explains a qualitative change in the distributional form and a sharp parameter sensitivity, rather than recalculating an arbitrary finite integral.
